name: grant_enforces_per_activity_cap_and_reserve_partition
description: admit's one-shot 60 KiB reserve is a partition separate from grant's ordinary bytes: grant may fill up to ORDINARY_CAP (PER_ACTIVITY_CAP - RESERVE = 4132864), one more byte is refused, and `reserved` never changes across any of it.

name: corrupt_ledger_entry_charged_full_per_activity_cap
description: A malformed ledger entry (unparseable JSON) is charged the FULL 4 MiB PER_ACTIVITY_CAP liability, never 0 and never a partial/estimated amount -- counters are never rebuilt from a corrupt file.

name: refuse_while_corrupt_at_real_ceiling
description: A corrupt entry that STANDS (its owner.lock held, so it cannot evidence-clear) makes admit AND grant refuse UNCONDITIONALLY -- not merely 'until capacity runs out'. Uses the REAL 64 MiB ceiling (never lowered): total charge here is far below it, so refusal can only be explained by the corrupt-entry gate, not capacity exhaustion.

name: terminal_durability_failure_preserves_reservation
description: B1: a synthesized terminal must be fsync'd durable BEFORE it is considered settled. When the segment fsync fails, synthesize-terminal returns false (not durable) and the ledger reservation is preserved for a future retry -- never lost.
